summary: You present a clear reef-monitoring rationale, a readable timetable in Image 1, and relevant sources in “Useful Links.” To strengthen the report, turn the broad mission functions into measurable design requirements, add interpreted technical results, and develop the plan and presentation to a more professional, mission-specific level.
next_steps: In “Mission Concept & Rationale,” define measurable coverage and performance requirements, then assess whether a proposed instrument can meet them, including spectral bands, resolution, water depth and turbidity. Clarify the acidification statistic: describe the change in hydrogen-ion concentration and corresponding pH decrease.

Move beyond research and STK tutorials in “Project Plan & Preliminary Progress”: include preliminary launch or orbit calculations, STK outputs and brief interpretations. To support near-real-time monitoring, analyse revisit, communications/downlink and latency requirements.

Build on Image 1 with contingency tasks and explain how the schedule’s design choices serve the reef-monitoring mission. For the next presentation level, use consistent bibliographic references and formal, grammatically polished writing throughout.

criteria.C1: “Mission Concept & Rationale” clearly identifies reef monitoring’s users and benefits, including marine and conservation scientists. To reach Accomplished, define specific mission requirements and show how instrument capabilities, coverage and performance targets meet those needs. Also assess the proposed seafloor colour/tone method and describe ocean acidification precisely as increased hydrogen-ion concentration with a corresponding pH decrease.
criteria.C2: Image 1 and the task descriptions provide a plausible timetable, and “Useful Links” identifies relevant sources. To reach Accomplished, add contingency provision and explain how the plan is tailored to the mission and how design choices will be evaluated or adjusted. Include the orbit/revisit, downlink and latency work needed to support the proposed near-real-time service.
criteria.C3: Your background research and completion of STK tutorials 1–4 show preparation. However, no preliminary calculations, launch/orbit analysis, simulations or interpreted technical results are presented. To progress, include useful technical work; the Accomplished level requires preliminary results with brief description or interpretation that demonstrate the project is on track.
criteria.C4: The report has clear headings, and Image 1 is a labelled, readable Gantt chart. To reach Accomplished, refine informal or awkward phrasing and make reference presentation consistent and properly bibliographic, ensuring citations in the text match the reference list. Maintain clear, consistent formatting for all figures and tables.
